limits: Python and libraries on this page: the page's own playground runs in your browser, in Python 3.13.2, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with pyttsx3 2.99, openai-whisper 20250625, yt-dlp 2026.8.19, torch 2.14.1 (CPU), NumPy 2.5.4, eSpeak NG 1.51 and ffmpeg 6.1.1 (and other releases where a section says so).

Recorded, not run: all 74 examples of the chapter. A browser's Python (its platform is 'emscripten') has no speech engine and no ffmpeg, does not have pyttsx3, Whisper or yt-dlp and cannot start programs (it raises OSError 'emscripten does not support processes'); each example is shown with its output recorded under Python 3.14.6, labelled 'Recorded, not run on this page', with its reason: AnswersAppendixB, BotCheck, BrokenSaveHangs, ChapterDigest, DefaultModelAnswer, DownloadCall, DriverAndLibrary, EmptyTextRefused, EspeakDependency, ExtensionIgnored, ExtractAudioPostprocessor, FailureStopsList, FfmpegRequired, FirstCallRace, GameSpoken, GetWriter, HumanReadings, InfoDictionary, KeysOfBook, LanguagesAndDetection, LinuxEspeak, MacNsss, MemoryAndGpuLimits, ModelFiles, ModelTimes, ModelWerTable, NoFfmpegDownload, NoSoundCard, NotExecutedList, NotExecutedYoutube, NumbersSpoken, OfflineAnswer, OnlineMaterials, OutOfRangeValues, Pep594Modules, PersistentVoice, PinnedInstallFails, PinnedReleaseTruncates, PublicDomainSource, PythonSeries, Pyttsx3Package, PyttsxReleases, RateDuration, ReadBackCues, ResultStructure, RunAndWaitLoop, SanitizeInfo, SayQueuesText, SetPropertyQueued, SilenceHallucination, SingleRunLabels, SongAudio, SongLyrics, SongTranscribed, SpeakFunction, SrtListing, SrtToVtt, TextVersusBook, ThreeFormats, TimeFormats, TimestampGrid, TranscribeLoop, TsvListing, VoiceObjects, VolumeScale, VttListing, WavFormat, WhisperPackage, WhisperReleases, WindowsSapi5, WriterOptions, YouTubeTerms, YtDlpPackage, YtDlpReleases.

Pictures: 5 recorded pictures drawn by the deck's programs from audio that eSpeak NG spoke (under FfmpegRequired, RateDuration, ReadBackCues, SongAudio, WavFormat) are shown beside their examples, labelled 'Recorded picture, not made on this page'; they are SHA-256 checked when the page is made.

No wheel is embedded on this page, no Whisper model file and no file of the book's online materials (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes holding 91 files; hello_tts.py is the one that imports pyttsx3). The licence of the zip and of its files is an open question for the owner (03-materials/ch24/assets/ASSETS_PROVENANCE_v1_0_0.md).

Findings, not successes: transcription with the Whisper models medium and turbo was killed at about 6 GB of memory on the research machine, and large-v3 (3,087,371,615 bytes) does not load there; tiny, base and small ran (model_runtimes_v1_0_0.json).

NOT EXECUTED: sound playback (no sound card), a microphone, the GPU and CUDA, Windows SAPI5 and macOS NSSpeechSynthesizer (their drivers were read only), the cloud services (the OpenAI API, Google Cloud and Azure) and faster-whisper, whisper.cpp, SpeechRecognition, gTTS and Vosk (their pages were read only), downloads from YouTube (only metadata was requested), transcription with the medium, turbo and large-v3 models (the first two were killed by the memory limit of the machine at about 6 GB and the third does not load), the pinned openai-whisper releases that cannot install on Python 3.12, and the 9 pyttsx3 releases that crash with a segmentation fault and the 5 that need macOS.

What the public sites answered on 2026-10-14 is in live_observations_v1_0_0.json: the chapter's page (status 200, 44,667 bytes, equal to the digest in the book's ontology) and the book's other pages, PyPI and the Whisper model files; YouTube asked for metadata answered with a bot check and nothing was downloaded from it. The chapter pins pyttsx3 2.98 and openai-whisper 20231117 (Appendix A); the newest releases are 2.99 and 20250625.

One program was run under 11 interpreters (3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.14, 3.14.0, 3.14.1, 3.14.2, 3.14.3, 3.14.4, 3.14.5, 3.14.6, 3.15.0b4): 2 of 14 items differ between them (the modules PEP 594 removed); the Whisper program under the same 11 interpreters (2 of 16 items differ). Releases: 22 of pyttsx3 (6 of 10 items differ), 13 of openai-whisper (7 of 11 items differ) and 6 of yt-dlp (2 of 8 items differ); see interpreter_record_v1_0_0.json. The chapter's 17 listings were replayed as 46 printed statements in four environments (34, 35, 8 and 32 of them match the book: newest, pinned, empty and no ffmpeg).
